subject: Physics
subtopic: Energy Density, Intensity and Momentum of Electromagnetic Waves
question: A linearly polarized electromagnetic wave propagates in vacuum with electric field $$\mathbf{E}=E_0\cos(kx-\omega t)\,\hat{y}$$ where the amplitude $E_0=300\,\text{V m}^{-1}$. A perfectly absorbing flat plate is placed perpendicular to the direction of propagation. What is the average radiation pressure exerted on the plate? (Answer to 2 significant figures in $\text{N m}^{-2}$)
explanation:
The intensity (average power per unit area) of a plane EM wave in vacuum is
$$I=\frac{1}{2}\,c\,\varepsilon_0\,E_0^{2}$$
where $c=3\times10^{8}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon_0=8.854\times10^{-12}\,\text{F m}^{-1}$.\
First compute $E_0^{2}= (300)^{2}=9.0\times10^{4}\,\text{V}^{2}\text{m}^{-2}$.\
\
$$\begin{aligned}
I&=\frac{1}{2}\times3\times10^{8}\times8.854\times10^{-12}\times9.0\times10^{4}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\times3\times10^{8}\times7.9686\times10^{-7}\\
&\approx\frac{1}{2}\times239.1\\
&\approx1.19\times10^{2}\,\text{W m}^{-2}\
\end{aligned}$$
For a perfectly absorbing surface the radiation pressure $p$ is related to intensity by $p=I/c$.\
\
$$p=\frac{1.19\times10^{2}}{3\times10^{8}}\approx3.97\times10^{-7}\,\text{N m}^{-2}$$\
Rounded to two significant figures, $p=4.0\times10^{-7}\,\text{N m}^{-2}$.
